title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Résolutions canoniques d'un groupe abélien'. The page sketches how to obtain a canonical (functorial) resolution of an abelian group G by free abelian groups on sets built from G. This is the tool needed on the neighbouring pages to compute H^*(K(G_a,n),G_a) and Ext's of G_a on the big site.

(1) Lines 1-2: a canonical augmented complex X_*(G) -> G whose terms are of the form Z[G^n x ...] (transcription uncertain). This is the type of resolution of Eilenberg–Mac Lane's Q-construction / Breen's resolution, with terms that are sums of Z[G^{n_i}]. Grothendieck also writes the cotriple (comonad) resolution of G for the free-abelian-group monad, Z[Z[G]] ⇉ Z[G] -> G. The note 'G -> G'' and 'H' indicates functoriality in G.

(2) Left margin: 'Pour tout n on a une résolution simpliciale de K(G,n)'. For the simplicial abelian group K(G,n) = G ⊗ (simplicial model of K(Z,n), i.e. Z~[S^n], Dold–Thom/Dold–Kan), the same cotriple gives ... Z[Z K(G,n)] ⇉ Z[K(G,n)] -> K(G,n). 'n grand' says one uses this in the stable range. Taking n large, a resolution of K(G,n) desuspends to a functorial resolution of G whose terms are built from Z[G^k].

(3) Main estimate. The previous page proves that K(Z,n) ∧ X -> Z~[S^n ∧ X] is a (2n-1)-quasi-isomorphism. Compose it with Z~ applied to the suspension map S^n ∧ K(G,p) -> K(G,n+p). That map is a homology isomorphism up to about degree n+2p, since H~_i K(G,p) is stable for i < 2p. The composite K(Z,n) ∧ K(G,p) -> Z K(G,n+p) is then an r-quasi-isomorphism with r = min(n+2p-1, 2n+p-1). This is the unstable shadow of HZ ∧ HG ≃ stable homology of K(G,·).

(4) Iteration. Suppose p_1+...+p_{r+1} = p. Repeating the construction gives K(Z,p_1) ∧ ... ∧ K(Z,p_r) ∧ K(G,p_{r+1}) -> Z^r K(G,p), the r-fold iterate of the free abelian group functor. The worked case r=2 is the vertical chain
K(Z,n)∧K(Z,m)∧K(G,p) -> Z[S^n∧K(Z,m)∧K(G,p)] -> Z[K(Z,n+m)∧K(G,p)] -> Z[Z[S^{n+m}∧K(G,p)]] -> Z[Z K(G,n+m+p)].
It uses S^n ∧ K(Z,m) -> K(Z,n+m) and then step (3) inside Z[-].

Purpose: in a stable range, identify the homotopy of the terms Z^r K(G,n) of the cotriple resolution with homotopy of smash products of Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces. Their homology is computable (Cartan), so the canonical resolution of K(G,n), and hence of G, becomes explicit. This is the input for computing the operations H^*(K(G_a,n),G_a) and Ext^*(G_a,G_a) on the next page.
errors: The free functor should be the reduced one Z~ = Z^+ (as on the previous page) throughout; writing Z K(G,n+p) or Z[S^n∧X] unreduced is slightly sloppy.

The connectivity bounds are only sketched (f(n,p) is first left unspecified, then given as min(n+2p-1, 2n+p-1)). Off-by-one conventions for 'r-quasi-isomorphism' are not fixed, and the iterated version's range is not stated.
The degree-shift bookkeeping in the iterated map to Z^r K(G,p) is implicit; nothing substantive appears wrong.

ideas.what: Canonical functorial resolution of an abelian group by free abelian groups on (powers of) the underlying set, obtained via the cotriple Z[-] and the stable range of K(G,n)
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Mac Lane Q-construction / Breen's canonical resolution (terms sums of Z[A^{n_i}])
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–Mac Lane (Q-construction, 1950s); L. Breen, 'Extensions du groupe additif', Publ. Math. IHÉS 48 (1978); later Mac Lane, Jibladze–Pirashvili

ideas.what: Cotriple simplicial resolution Z[Z[X]] ⇉ Z[X] -> X of a simplicial abelian group K(G,n)
ideas.modern_name: Free abelian group (Dold–Thom) cotriple resolution; Bousfield–Kan Z-resolution

ideas.what: K(Z,n) ∧ K(G,p) -> Z~K(G,n+p) is a quasi-isomorphism in the range min(n+2p-1, 2n+p-1)
ideas.modern_name: Stable-range identification HZ ∧ HG ≃ Σ^∞ stable homology of EM spaces; Freudenthal-type estimate
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–Mac Lane, Cartan (stable homology of EM spaces); standard

ideas.what: Iterated version: smash of K(Z,p_i)'s with K(G,p_{r+1}) maps quasi-isomorphically (stably) to the r-fold iterate Z^r K(G,p)
ideas.modern_name: Identification of E1-terms of the Z-homology (Bousfield–Kan / unstable Adams) resolution with smash products of EM spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck is independently sketching, around his 1976 IHÉS lecture, the method Breen published in 1978. Breen's method builds a canonical resolution of an abelian group (sheaf) by sums of Z[A^n] from stable-range comparisons of EM spaces, in order to compute Ext(G_a,G_a). This documents Grothendieck's direct engagement with this circle of ideas but does not appear to add a result absent from the literature.
missed.quote: Pour tout n on a une résolution simpliciale de K(G,n) ... n grand ... r = min(n+2p-1, 2n+p-1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck working through the Breen/Eilenberg–Mac Lane approach to Ext of G_a, relevant to dating and attribution in the history of Breen's 'Extensions du groupe additif'.

deep.surprise_reason: Competent working notes reconstructing a known technique: Eilenberg–Mac Lane/Breen canonical resolution via stable homology of EM spaces and cotriple resolutions. Mathematically standard and credited elsewhere; mild historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Z^{Z^G} ⇉ Z^G is Grothendieck's exponent notation for Z[Z[G]] ⇉ Z[G] (the cotriple resolution), not a power set.
Likewise Z^{Z K(G,n)} ⇉ Z^{K(G,n)} means Z[Z[K(G,n)]] ⇉ Z[K(G,n)].
In the first smash map the first factor is K(Z,n) (the machine reading 'K(B,n)' is a corrected slip).
'K(G,n) = G ⊗_Z Λ^n ψ': Λ^n ψ appears to be Grothendieck's notation for the simplicial free abelian model of K(Z,n) (same notation on the next page, G_a ⊗ (Λ^n ψ)); the reading is uncertain.
The definition of X_*(G) (first line, 'Z(G^n × Z^+)') is uncertain in the image; it plausibly denotes terms of the form Z[G^n × ...].
